description.en:
Not a function a script can call: an identifier of the game's message (dialogue text) parser.
It exists only as a symbol string in the game's ELF binary, lxpCMessage::DATA::CMND_NONE. That makes it a value of an enum named DATA inside the lxpCMessage class, the list of control codes the parser recognises inside message text (ruby, line breaks, waits, colours and so on; see the other CMND_* message tags).
It is not registered as a Squirrel function and appears nowhere in the shipped scripts. Going by its name it is most likely the "no control code" value, plain text; its byte-level encoding was not traced.
The fifteen names of that enum appear together in the binary, CMND_NONE first, followed by CMND_CHAR, CMND_CHAR_RUBI, CMND_RUBI, CMND_RUBI_END, CMND_GAIJI, CMND_LINE, CMND_WAIT, CMND_TOUCH_WAIT, CMND_SKIP_START, CMND_SKIP_END, CMND_COLOR_START, CMND_COLOR_END, CMND_COLOR_RUBI_START and CMND_COLOR_RUBI_END. That order is probably the enum order, which would make CMND_NONE value 0 (not confirmed).
Not applicable: this is not a callable function. Calling CMND_NONE from a script would fail because no such global exists.
